items.x_text:
Optimizely supply-chain attack: malicious JavaScript served via Optimizely Web to 178 organisations on 16 Nov, per Report URI's Scott Helme. It swapped crypto wallets and skimmed cards. Only 24 had a CSP strict enough to block it.

items.ig_caption:
178 organisations. One trusted script. 🧩

What Help Net Security and Malwarebytes reported (17 Nov):
→ On 16 Nov, malicious JavaScript was served through Optimizely Web to visitors of 178 organisations, per Scott Helme of Report URI
→ Optimizely says "an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation" to add it to some customer projects; it has fixed the flaw and removed the code
→ The code swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed cards typed into sites' own payment forms, and stole cookies and screenshots
→ Helme's list includes Zoom, BBC, CNN, HSBC and IKEA; delivery of iOS exploit kits was seen, but no iPhone compromise has been demonstrated
→ Only 24 organisations had a CSP strict enough to block it; 68 had none, and allow-listing Optimizely's domain didn't help

My take: allow-listing a vendor's domain isn't control if the vendor gets hit. I'd inventory every third-party script on payment pages and keep them off checkout where I can.

What to do (site owners): tighten your CSP, review vendor script settings that enable eval, and monitor what third-party scripts actually do. Visitors: update iOS and check card and crypto activity from 16 Nov.
